clue.text: Detective, seeing that curtailed course, is put off

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: seeing that means since, as in 'given that'
a line is a course or route taken

explanation.surface: A detective is unsettled because a course of study was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To disincline someone is to make them unwilling, which is what deterring them does.

clue.text: He'll give you such a different expression

definitions.text: He'll give you such a different expression

parts.words: He'll give you such a different expression
parts.note: He is the chemical symbol of the gas whose inhaling makes the voice squeaky, so 'He' giving a changed way of talking is literal

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'He' as the chemical symbol for the light gas from party balloons; breathing it in raises the pitch of your voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the comic high-pitched voice produced after inhaling the lighter-than-air gas.

clue.text: Henry's off cannabis, limiting vacation

indicators.note: off means taken away, so this letter leaves the word for the drug

parts.note: hemp is the plant cannabis
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
tying means binding or restricting

explanation.surface: Henry has given up cannabis and is restricting his holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' here is the act of vacating, not a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacation in its older sense is the act of vacating or clearing out, the same as making something empty.

clue.text: Picked up narrative about hot temperature, making you horrified

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for hot goes within
in a down clue, picked up means lifted so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a saga is a long narrative
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Hearing a story about the heat leaves someone horrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast describes someone filled with shock and dismay, close to horrified.

clue.text: Upholding a boy exercising a portion of the brain

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means the string is raised so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy
gym, as in a school PE lesson, stands for exercising

explanation.surface: Someone supports a lad who is working out a part of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond-shaped cluster deep in the temporal lobe is a structure of the brain linked to emotion.

clue.text: Formerly suspended, one's dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the letter for one leaves the phrase

parts.note: on ice means put on hold, suspended
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone formerly suspended has now been sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, a synonym of formerly.

clue.text: Power worker to get on with operatives, keeping ahead of tense hierarchical structure

indicators.note: keeping ahead of means staying in front, so the operatives come before the tense letter

parts.note: a lineman repairs overhead electricity cables
to get on is to grow older, to age
operatives are workers, men
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An electricity worker gets along with colleagues while keeping ahead of a tense workplace hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Line management is the chain of command in which each employee reports to a manager above, a ranked structure.

clue.text: See 7
Reading now, shocked about court in Japanese novel

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the word for court
shocked hair is tousled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: to court is to woo

explanation.surface: Someone reading at this moment is shocked by a court case in a Japanese novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' rearranges READINGNOW into NORWEGIAN plus D, which goes 'about' WOO to finish NORWEGIAN WOO D.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1987 book by Haruki Murakami, named after a Beatles song, a Japanese work of fiction.

clue.text: Title adopted by popular churchman

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the two words are combined one within the other

parts.note: Mister is a title before a man's name
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A popular clergyman takes on a formal title.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

clue.text: One having a way of looking at river

definitions.note: one here is a person, the fisher by the river

parts.note: an angle is a point of view, a way of looking at things
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone has a particular way of looking at the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is a person who fishes, so 'one' here stands for that person sitting on the bank.

clue.text: Seafood racket's very good

parts.note: a racket is a fraudulent scheme, a scam
pi is short for pious, very good

explanation.surface: A seafood fraud is said to be excellent business.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a classic shellfish dish.

clue.text: Minor actor having difficulty with fruity material

parts.note: an extra is a non-speaking film actor
a jam is a tight spot, a difficulty

explanation.surface: A bit-part player has trouble with some fruit-flavoured stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra jam is the grade of preserve made with a higher proportion of fruit, a fruity spread.

clue.text: A new corporation importing English alarm of prewar design

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the letters go inside the word for a belly

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum
a bell is an alarm

explanation.surface: A new company brings in an English alarm system built before the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old humorous word for a large stomach, hence TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Antebellum literally means before the war, used of buildings and style from before the US Civil War.

clue.text: New arrangement for financing? It is irrelevant

indicators.note: a new arrangement of letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a new finance deal matters, and is told it does not.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insignificant is too small or unimportant to matter, so beside the point.

clue.text: Our calf's butchered for consumption

indicators.note: butchered means cut up and mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our calf is slaughtered so that it can be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumption' looks like eating, but it is the old name for tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrofula is tuberculosis of the neck glands, and consumption is the old word for tuberculosis.

clue.text: I'm taking drug to part of hospital that's without power

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A patient on drugs heads to a hospital ward that has had a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotent means powerless, unable to act effectively.

clue.text: Make a mistake in recording, missing last turtle

indicators.note: in means placed within the other word
missing last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taping is recording
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone slips up while recording and misses the final shot of a turtle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing last' cuts TAPING to TAPIN, and ERR goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle.

clue.text: Fourth suggestion about old European state

indicators.note: about means around, so the plan surrounds the letter for old

parts.note: a plan is a proposal or suggestion
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A fourth proposal concerns an old European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth' comes first in the clue but its letter D ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Poland is a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Overlook British invading chic area of Paris

indicators.note: invading means entering, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Passy is a smart district of Paris's 16th arrondissement

explanation.surface: British people invade a fashionable Parisian district.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass by something is to ignore or disregard it, as to overlook it.

clue.text: See 2
Unhappy with oil, initially changing fuel

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the two words
changing means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy about switching fuel to oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Woeful means full of sorrow, wretched.

clue.text: Work over: turn up to drink

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the word is flipped to read bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Revise some work, then show up for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition.

clue.text: Honestly? Otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doubting 'Honestly?' is answered with 'No, the opposite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something secretly is the opposite of acting openly and honestly, so it is honest conduct turned the other way.

clue.text: Note university working with dull BBC lingo — it's a controversial university group

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: n is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's dreary jargon is blended into a remark about a university society.
explanation.walkthrough: The BULLINGDON CLUB is a notorious Oxford dining society whose members have included British prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: This Oxford dining society is notorious for rowdy, wealthy members, making it a contentious student association.
